frequency_question: How often do sovereign debt management scaling schedules successfully meet their target throughput volume increments within a designated 105-day operational window without calendar slippage?
membership_rule: Includes any announced multi-tranche sovereign debt buyback or liquidity injection scaling program by a major developed market treasury/central bank where volume per operation was scheduled to step up over a defined horizon. Excludes emergency ad-hoc interventions.

cases.name: Federal Reserve QE tapering/scaling acceleration phases (2013-2014)
Bank of England gilt purchase operation volume adjustments (2022)
US Treasury initial rollout of regular Treasury buybacks (2024)
ECB PEPP monthly purchase volume scaling phases (2020)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major central bank/treasury operational scaling windows examined; believed to represent the universe of directly comparable transparent debt management scaling intervals in recent decades.
known_gaps: Limited sample size due to the rarity of regular large-scale sovereign buyback program introductions.
skeleton: 4 named sovereign operational scaling execution phases across major jurisdictions representing institutional implementation of debt management changes.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 observed structured programmatic scaling windows.
validity_reason: Treasury and central bank operational processing capacity and bureaucratic lead times evolve slowly over multi-year technological horizons.
